title: 第25章 售后服务第26章 他真是个好人
slug: 转生反派贵族妈妈们都太爱我了
content_zh:
;;
马车没走远，就在城外三里的一处废弃磨坊旁停下了。
这里野草疯长，平时只有野狗和流浪汉光顾，现在却成了临时的营地。
那个巨大的铁笼被卸在草地上，像是个沉重的黑色棺材。
塞拉菲娜蜷缩在笼子的一角，双手抱着膝盖。
那件破烂的丝绸裙子挡不住夜风，她冷得牙齿打颤，但更让她不安的是那个买了她的男人。
从出了奴隶市场到现在，整整两个小时，那个出售阔卓的年轻人没跟她说过一句话。
既没有那种急不可耐的扑上来，也没有那种变态的羞辱。
他只是让人把笼子扔在这，然后就自顾自地坐在篝火旁，拿着一块干硬的面包在烤。
这种未知的等待，比鞭子更折磨人。
“你要干什么？”塞拉菲娜终于忍不住了，带着一股子强撑的硬气，“如果是想我向你摇尾乞怜，那你还是趁早杀了我。”
肖恩头都没回，撕下一块烤热的面包塞进嘴里，嚼得起劲，又喝一口壶里的奶。
飘香四溢。
这种无视让塞拉菲娜感到一种久违的挫败感。
天色彻底暗了下来。
肖恩拍了拍手上的面包屑，终于站了起来。
他走到正在擦拭盾牌的沃恩身边。
“沃恩。”
“少爷。”沃恩立刻放下盾牌，站得笔直。
“记得那家铺子吗？”肖恩指了指灰石城的方向，“去查查底细，那个拿着鞭子吆喝的小贩，还有那个躲在后面数钱的胖老板，以及店里所有的伙计，股东。”

沃恩那张粗犷的脸上没有任何表情波动，只是点了点头：“都要活的？”
“都要活的。”肖恩顿了顿，又补充了一句，“除了带不过来的。”
“明白。”
沃恩转身点了十名骑士。
马蹄上裹了布，一行人像是融入黑夜的幽灵，悄无声息地朝着灰石城折返。
这一幕把旁边的伊莎贝拉看愣了。
她把早已熟睡的莱拉安顿在马车里，小心翼翼地走到肖恩身后，双手绞着衣角，犹豫了好半天才开口。
“那个……肖恩？”
“嗯？”
“你这是……要干什么？”伊莎贝拉看了一眼笼子里那个瑟瑟发抖的红发女人，又看了看杀气腾腾远去的骑士队，小声问道，“你已经花了五百金币把她买下来了，为什么还要……”
肖恩转过身，突然笑了一下。
火光映在他脸上，让那个笑容看起来有些意味深长。
“伊莎贝拉oo，你要知道一件事。”
肖恩伸出一根手指，在伊莎贝拉面前晃了晃，“我不喜欢浪费。”
“五百金币，那可是我们领地半年的税收。”
“我这人，没有乱花钱的习惯。”
伊莎贝拉眨了眨眼，没听懂。
但看着肖恩那双黑沉沉的眼睛，她本能地把剩下的疑问咽了回去。
夜越来越深。
荒野上的风声像鬼哭。

塞拉菲娜靠在铁栏杆上，眼皮哪怕再沉重，也不敢真的睡过去。

The carriage did not go far and stopped beside an abandoned mill three miles outside the city.
Weeds have grown wildly here, and usually only wild dogs and homeless people visit it, but now it has become a temporary camp.
The huge iron cage was unloaded on the grass, like a heavy black coffin.
Serafina huddled in a corner of the cage, holding her knees with her hands.
The tattered silk skirt could not block the night wind, and her teeth chattered with the cold, but what made her even more uneasy was the man who bought her.
From the time she left the slave market to now, for two whole hours, the young man who sold Kuozhuo had not said a word to her.
There was neither the impatient rush nor the perverted humiliation.
He just asked people to throw the cage here, and then he sat by the campfire and baked a piece of dry bread.
This unknown waiting is more torturous than the whip.
"What are you going to do?" Serafina finally couldn't bear it anymore and said with a strong spirit, "If you want me to beg for mercy from you, then you'd better kill me as soon as possible."
Without turning his head, Sean tore off a piece of toasted bread and stuffed it into his mouth. He chewed it vigorously and took another sip of milk from the jug.
The fragrance overflows.
This disregard made Serafina feel a long-lost sense of frustration.
The sky turned completely dark.
Sean patted the crumbs on his hands and finally stood up.
He walked over to Vaughn, who was wiping his shield.
"Vaughn."
"Master." Vaughn immediately put down his shield and stood up straight.
"Remember that shop?" Sean pointed in the direction of Greystone City, "Go and find out the details, the hawker who was shouting with a whip, the fat boss who was hiding behind and counting money, and all the clerks and shareholders in the shop."
There was no expression on Vaughn's rough face, and he just nodded: "All alive?"
"Everyone is alive." Sean paused and added, "Except those who can't be brought here."
"Understood."
Vaughn turned around and ordered ten knights.
The horses' hooves were wrapped in cloth, and the group of people turned back toward Graystone City silently like ghosts blending into the night.
This scene stunned Isabella next to her.
She put Laila, who was already asleep, in the carriage, walked carefully behind Sean, wrung her clothes with her hands, and hesitated for a long time before speaking.
"That... Sean?"
"Huh?"
"What...are you going to do?" Isabella glanced at the trembling red-haired woman in the cage, then at the knights who were fleeing with murderous intent, and asked in a low voice, "You have already spent five hundred gold coins to buy her, why do you still..."
Sean turned around and smiled suddenly.
The firelight reflected on his face made that smile look meaningful.
"Isabella, you need to know one thing."
Sean stretched out a finger and waved it in front of Isabella, "I don't like waste."
"Five hundred gold coins, that's half a year's tax revenue for our territory."
"I don't have the habit of spending money carelessly."
Isabella blinked, not understanding.
But looking at Sean's dark eyes, she instinctively swallowed back the remaining questions.
The night is getting deeper and deeper.
The sound of wind in the wilderness is like the cry of ghosts.
Serafina leaned against the iron railing, no matter how heavy her eyelids were, she didn't dare to really fall asleep.
